- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (especially if sentiment drops post-spike) — adjust downward bias.
- Overshoot near end of forecast horizon (especially 28–30 days) — apply early mean reversion correction.
- When sentiment is low (< 0.3) and price is falling, model tends to underestimate — add 2–3% buffer to avoid bottoming too early.
- If sentiment is volatile or oscillating, avoid sharp directional forecasts — favor smoother, trend-following adjustments.
- Model overreacts to recent spikes — dampen momentum in forecast if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is consistently low, expect downward drift — adjust forecast slope downward.
